final_synthesis:
Electric vehicles (EVs) are often touted for their environmental benefits, particularly regarding greenhouse gas emissions [S4]. According to recent studies, battery electric cars registered in Europe in 2021 have life-cycle greenhouse gas emissions that are 66-69% lower than comparable petrol cars [S1]. This significant reduction is due to the overall lifecycle analysis which includes both manufacturing and operational phases. Initial manufacturing impacts, especially from batteries, contribute higher emissions early on; these 'carbon debts' are repaid within about one to two years of typical driving [S1].

The climate advantage of electric vehicles depends heavily on the carbon intensity of the electricity grid they use [S2]. In regions with coal-heavy grids, the life-cycle emission reduction is less pronounced but still generally lower than petrol cars. As more electricity comes from renewable sources, EVs' emissions advantages continue to grow [S3].

Moreover, EVs release no tailpipe pollutants and can reduce respiratory illnesses like asthma by decreasing air pollution types such as nitrogen dioxide [S4].
